units: Deut. VI, 4) Sh’mʿa, the confession of faith in the morning and evening prayers (recitation of Deut. VI, 4-9; XI, 13-21; Num. XVI, 37-41).
<cite ref="Targum Jonathan on Numbers 25:6">Targ. Y. I Num. XXV, 6</cite>. Targ. II Esth. III, 8.—

Ber. I, 1 מאימתי קורין את ש׳ וכ׳ from what time of the day may we read the Sh’mʿa of the evening prayer? Ib. II, 2 (13ᵃ) למה קדמה (פרשת) ש׳ וכ׳ why does the reading of the section of Sh’mʿa (Deut. VI, 4–9) precede that of v’hayah (ib. XI, 13-21) Ib. בין שניה לש׳ ובין ש׳ וכ׳ between the second benediction and Sh’mʿa (the first section), and between Sh’mʿa and v’hayah &c.; a. fr.—קריאת ש׳ (abbr. ק״ש), v. קְרִיאָה. Ib. 2ᵃ ק״ש דשכיבה the recitation of Sh’mʿa at bed-time.

<cite ref="Bamidbar Rabbah 20:21">Num. R. s. 20<sup>20</sup></cite> <he>עומדין … וחוטפין ק״ש וכ׳</he> they rise from their sleep like lions, and hasten to read the Sh’mʿa, and proclaim the kingship of the Lord &c.
<cite ref="Bamidbar Rabbah 20:21">Ib.</cite> <he>והוא … בק״ש משומרי וכ׳</he> and with the recital of the Sh’mʿa he is handed over from the guards of the day to those of the night.
<cite ref="Berakhot 4b:27">Ber. 4ᵇ</cite> <he>אע״פ שקרא אדם ק״ש וכ׳</he> although one has read the Sh. in synagogue, it is proper to recite it again on going to bed.
<cite ref="Berakhot 5a:5">Ib. 5ᵃ</cite> <he>אם … ואם לאו יקרא ק״ש</he> if he conquers it (the evil thought), it is well, and if not, let him read the Sh.; a. v. fr.
